featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
Revival is one of those places that quietly delivers on everything you expect from a comforting dining experience. With its sea facing setting and focus on Pure Veg and Jain food, it is a spot that naturally lends itself to relaxed family outings.

A recent visit was centred around their Summer Special Mango Menu, which brings in a refreshing seasonal touch. The Kairi Kanda Roomali and Pakoda made for a great start and disappeared almost instantly. The Paneer Kairi Tikka stood out with its soft texture and well balanced flavours, easily one of the highlights from the menu.

The beverage selection complements the theme well. Options like the Mango Frozen Margarita and Mango Passion Fruit Mojito are refreshing, while the Mango Lassi is a great pick if you are in the mood for something richer and more filling.

Moving to the mains, the Paneer Khada Masala with Garlic leaves a strong impression and ranks among the better versions you will come across. It fits perfectly into the kind of comforting, flavourful food this place is known for.

Desserts keep things traditional and satisfying. The Gulab Jamun paired with Lacchedar Rabdi works beautifully, while the Aamras Puri is an easy choice, especially during the season.

What makes Revival stand out is how easy it is to return to. It is the kind of place that works just as well for a casual meal as it does for a family outing, and even welcomes your furry companions.

Conveniently located a short walk from Charni Road station, and set within a heritage building just off the Chowpatty seaface, it is a spot that is both accessible and consistently dependable when you are in the mood for good, comforting food.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Nayan Bheda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointing Experience on Diwali
We were a group of 5 who had booked a table a day in advance through Google for 20th Oct, 9pm. On calling the restaurant in the afternoon about parking, the manager suddenly claimed they have “stopped online reservations” — even though the slot was available and confirmed on Google. When I asked his name (atleast thriceA) he disconnected the call without telling.
Not taking a chance, we reached at 7:30pm. The restaurant was barely 40% occupied. Our waiter Kabir was polite and helpful — full marks to him for service.
The major issue happened at billing — they flatly refused to accept Zomato payment despite Zomato showing a good discount option. There was no notice displayed, and we were not told at entry or while ordering. The manager “Shrikant Pedhnekar” was unapologetic and defensive instead of clarifying or expressing regret. While we were leaving, another manager (name unknown) also argued with us. In this era of 'Customer First', not once these managers showed any signs of being apologetic nor regret. The high-handed attitude spoiled our mood. Especially when the prices are comparable with premium restaurants. While prices match that of premium restaurant, the customer-centric attitude does not.

Other aspects:
• Ambience feels dated — furniture and décor easily 15–20 years old
• Prices are comparable to premium restaurants but food is only average in taste and portion
• We ordered for two cocktails but they were not well made.
• Service charge of 10% was added automatically while most restaurants of this level charge 5% (we got it removed)
• Restaurant is on 1st floor - No lift so elderlies and people with mobility issues will find it difficult to reach the restaurant

Overall, good food and smiling service of Kabir the waiter saved complete disaster. One star is for him. 4 stars goes out for an unprofessional and disappointing handling of guests. Would not recommend until management fixes confirmed reservations, billing transparency and how they treat their customers.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you for sharing your detailed feedback. We sincerely apologize for the issues you faced with reservations, billing, and management, and will take steps to improve our service and guest experience.

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.name: Manikandan
featured_reviews.review_text: Santosham - Satvik South Indian Restaurant near Marine Drive is a clean and comforting spot for authentic South Indian vegetarian food in South Mumbai. The restaurant keeps a simple, traditional feel without trying to be overly fancy, and the food is the main highlight. Located in Marine Lines, it’s convenient after a walk along Marine Drive or nearby sightseeing. Service is quick, portions are satisfying, and the overall experience feels homely and consistent without being overpriced. One amazing thing is they serve meals and rice items throughout the day even at night.

featured_reviews.name: Gaurangi Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text: It was truly one of the best South Indian dining experiences I’ve had. The podi idli and the mini idlis with curry leaf powder were absolutely exceptional, rich in flavour, beautifully aromatic, and completely addictive. The dosa was perfectly crisp, the food overall was immaculate, the service was warm and attentive, and the ambience was stunning and thoughtfully designed. featured_reviews.name: RACHNA TULI MASHKARIA
featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

We ordered dosa, uttapam, pizza, and pav bhaji. Unfortunately, the food didn’t meet our expectations. My mother felt the pav bhaji lacked flavor—as the saying goes, “unchi dukan, fiki pakwan” (big shop, bland food). Having tried authentic South Indian cuisine in Chennai and Kerala, I found Sukh Sagar’s dosa and uttapam fell short of that standard. The only dish that impressed us was the pizza.

The prices seemed quite high considering the taste and quality of the food. My mother, a senior citizen and excellent cook herself, jokingly remarked that she could prepare better food at home!

We will never come to this restaurant again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Iconic restaurant located at Charni Road, perhaps needs no introduction, was in the vicinity and was craving for some yummy Chaat and fast food! Shiv Krishna was our stop for that night. Named after two deities, one can expect it to be an all veg restaurant. The moment you enter the restaurant you can see beautiful paintings of Lord Krishna in various a avatars all over. Restaurant has two levels, upper deck has AC.

Talking about what all we had at Shiv Krishna -

As mentioned earlier was craving for some Chaat so we started with Sev Puri. Neatly presented to us. Sev Puri is usually famous of all street vendors and hawkers in Mumbai but you get a similar taste of it sitting in the comforts of this place. We followed it up with Veg Pizza. I would personally say it's made in the Indian way and I have no qualms in saying that I love the pizza made in this style. Very homely style and I enjoyed it.

Along with food, we ordered for couple of drinks - Paan Mojito and Kit Kat Shake. Mojito was refreshing with fresh Paan flavor. Good part is no essence. Kit Kat Shake was decent. Moving on, we next tried the famous Pav Bhaji of Shiv Sagar. It definitely features amongst the top selling list and most popular dish. Again presented in a very neat way. Was pretty stuffed by now, but the manager suggested us to also try the Tandoori Cheese Kulcha which is a relatively new dish introduced by the restaurant. Served in a starter format, so quite unique in its way. Stuffing is a mix of paneer and cheese mashed well and grilled well. Stuffed in Kulcha covering and kept in tandoor. Would recommend people to try this dish in case they haven't tried it elsewhere.

Last but not the least, was really excited to have the Cassatta ice-cream. Have had it really long back and was excited to see it as a part of the menu here. A combo of chocolate, tutti fruti, butter scotch ice-cream with nuts used for garnishing. Just loved the ice-cream and would love to revisit the place just for this again.

featured_reviews.name: Kiyansh Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vanakkam Vihar, located right opposite the iconic Royal Opera House in Girgaon, is a reliable, bustling spot for anyone craving solid, comforting South Indian comfort food in South Mumbai. Whether you are wrapping up a beach stroll at nearby Girgaon Chowpatty or stepping out after a show at the Opera House, this multi-level pure-vegetarian restaurant offers a welcoming and clean environment.
Here is a comprehensive look at what to expect:
The Vibe & Ambiance
The restaurant balances traditional charm with a modern, spacious casual-dining setup. The ground floor features comfortable high and low seating, while the upper level ("Firangi") branches out into multi-cuisine options. The space is well-lit, fully air-conditioned, and remarkably clean, making it highly family-friendly. The staff adds a touch of authenticity by dressing in traditional South Indian attire.
What to Order
While the massive menu extends to North Indian dishes and street-side snacks, the absolute highlight here remains their coastal and southern delicacies.
The Dosas: Their Kara Masala Dosa and Chettinad Dosa are beautifully crisp, served with generous portions of fresh coconut chutney, a tangy tomato-garlic chutney, and piping hot sambar. If you are looking for something lighter, the Neer Dosa and fluffy Appams paired with a rich veggie stew or Malabari curry are top-tier.
The Idli Platters: Beyond standard idlis, their Podi Idli (tossed in a vibrant, spiced gun powder and ghee) and the signature Thalaiva Idli are highly recommended.
Filter Coffee: No meal here is complete without their authentic Filter Coffee. It is served strong, perfectly frothy, and features that robust, traditional chicory-coffee blend.
Jain Options: For those with dietary restrictions, the restaurant stands out for offering a robust, dedicated selection of highly flavorful Jain South Indian variants.

What made our experience even more special was the staff. They are incredibly gentle, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. The hospitality here stands out. They pay attention to every detail and make sure you feel comfortable and taken care of. Whether it was helping us choose dishes or checking in to make sure everything was perfect, their service was warm and sincere. We were visiting Mumbai from outside the city for just four days, and we ended up eating at Golden Chimney four out of five days — that says everything. When you find a place that combines amazing food with outstanding hospitality, you naturally want to return. Every time we came back, the quality was consistent and impressive.
The money we spent was absolutely worth it.
The portion sizes, the flavor, the cleanliness, and the service all reflect great value for the price.

If you're in Mumbai and want authentic, flavorful food with heartfelt hospitality, Golden Chimney is a must-visit. We will definitely return the next time we are in the city.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Highly Disappointing Maharashtrian Food
Overall Rating: 3/10 (Based primarily on food Taste and facilities)
My recent visit to Vinay in Girgaon was a profound disappointment, particularly for anyone seeking authentic, high-quality Maharashtrian snacks. The experience was marred by poor execution of core dishes and subpar facilities, resulting in one of the worst quick-service dining experiences I've had in a while.
The Food Verdict
The most critical failure of the visit was the Misal Pav.
• Misal Pav: 1/10
This was, quite frankly, one of the worst Misal Pavs I have ever encountered. It lacked the characteristic spice, texture, and authentic flavor profile that defines this Maharashtrian staple. It was sweet 😂. If Misal is your purpose for visiting, please look elsewhere.
• Other Dishes: 3/10 (Okish)
We also sampled the Sabudana Wada, Vatana Pattice, and Veg Biryani. While these items were merely "okish," they still scored a very low 3 out of 10. They lacked freshness, or any distinguishing quality to warrant a recommendation or even a second thought.
Ambiance and Facilities
On a positive note, the restaurant offers good sitting options, including both AC and Non-AC sections, which is a rare plus point in this category.
However, the facility challenges are severe:
• Parking: There is no dedicated parking available, which can be a significant hassle in the congested Girgaon area.
• Toilets: The washroom facilities were, without exaggeration, the worst. This is a major area needing immediate attention and upkeep.
Final Recommendation
If your goal is to experience good, authentic, and delicious Maharashtrian cuisine, do not visit Vinay. You will be better served by traveling a little further to established names.
Alternative Recommendations for Authentic Maharashtrian Food:
• Misal Pav: For a truly great Misal, visit Mamledar Misal (Thane).
• General Maharashtrian Cuisine: For excellent, reliable snacks and meals, Prakash Shuddh Upahar Kendra (Dadar) remains a gold standard.

We went to Flavors at Bay near Hotel Hira mainly because it was convenient for us. Unfortunately, the food was a big disappointment.

We ordered momos, and they were honestly the worst part of the meal. They didn’t taste like real momos at all. Instead of a proper filling, it felt like a dough ball stuffed with pure spices. The taste matched how it looked — just overwhelming masala with no balance. Coming from a Nepali background where we eat momos often, this was really disappointing.

The service itself was good and the staff were polite. The location was convenient for us as well. However, the restaurant felt quite empty and overall the food experience was not good. Unfortunately, the heavy spices even gave us heartburn afterwards.

featured_reviews.name: Atul Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went for a Sunday brunch, and the restaurant manages to strike a nice balance between being busy and still feeling comfortable. The ambience is simple yet pleasant, with ample seating available in both AC and non-AC sections. Despite the steady crowd, the space feels organized and welcoming.

Since it was a Sunday, there was a queue when I arrived, and the waiting time was around 25 to 30 minutes before getting seated. However, the seating turnover is quite efficient, and once seated the service moves quickly. The overall setup works well for a place that sees such heavy footfall.

The Food
Rava Masala Dosa (Ghee): This was exactly what you would expect from a good South Indian restaurant, earning 3.8 to 4 out of 5. The dosa had the right texture and flavor profile.

Ulundu Dosa: Made primarily with urad dal, this dosa had a very distinct flavor. While it may appeal to those who enjoy that strong taste, it personally didn’t work for me as much, which places it at 2.5 out of 5.

Davangere Benne Dosa (with Cheese): This was something different from the usual dosa offerings. The flavor was again quite distinct, but it still carried an interesting richness and character. Overall, it lands at about 3 out of 5.

Bisibele Bath: This was a pleasant addition to the meal, earning 3.5 out of 5. The flavor was quite good, with the comforting, mildly spiced profile you expect from a well-made bisibele bath. However, the portion size felt noticeably small, which slightly took away from the overall experience. Taste-wise it delivered, but a larger serving would have made it far more satisfying.

Sides
Kothimbir Vadi: A tasty accompaniment that scored 3.5 out of 5. The flavor was enjoyable, though the preparation felt slightly oily.

Sabudana Vada: This was one of the highlights among the sides, easily earning 4.5 out of 5. The texture and flavor worked very well, making it a standout snack.

Beverage
Filter Coffee: Surprisingly, the coffee felt fairly average compared to the rest of the meal. It was decent but not particularly memorable, coming in at 3 out of 5.

Dessert
Mysore Pak: This was easily the best part of the entire meal. Rich, indulgent, and incredibly satisfying, it completely stole the show. If ratings allowed it, this would easily be a 10 out of 5.

Sambar & Chutney
Considering Ramashraya’s reputation, both the sambar and coconut chutney felt fairly average. They complemented the dishes but did not particularly stand out.

Overall Verdict
For a total bill of around ₹550, Ramashraya offers a solid dining experience with a wide variety of traditional South Indian options. While some dishes had very distinct flavor profiles that may not appeal to everyone, items like the Sabudana Vada and especially the Mysore Pak make the visit worthwhile. If you do visit, make sure you don’t leave without trying the Mysore Pak—it’s easily the highlight of the meal.

The restaurant has a simple, old-school vibe, but that’s part of its charm. Despite being crowded most of the time, the service is quick and efficient. It is located at a walkable distance from charni road station, which makes it very convenient to visit.
We tried some of their signature dishes, including ghee podi masala dosa, benne dosa, and sweet Mysore pak. Each dish was packed with flavor and tasted absolutely delicious. The Mysore pak was another highlight—soft, rich, and perfectly sweet, making it a great way to end the meal. One of the best things about this place is that the food is budget-friendly despite its high quality, which makes it a favorite among students and locals.
Overall, Ram Ashraya is a must-visit spot if you’re craving authentic South Indian food in Mumbai. Whether you’re going for breakfast or a quick meal, this place won’t disappoint. Highly recommended for anyone looking for tasty, affordable, and satisfying South Indian dishes!
